LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 13.3.1 WH- QUESTIONS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.3: Language Use 13.3.1 Wh- questions
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 13.3.1 Wh- questions, part of Strand 13 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we ask for information?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 13.3.1 Wh- questions together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: Skill of Speaking and Signing when the learner engages in meaningful question and answer dialogues using

Wh-words and signs in pairs/small groups.

● Self-efficacy: as learners gain the mastery of asking questions using the Wh- words.

Values:
Unity is fostered as the learner takes turns during dialogues with peers

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Citizenship: Social cohesion as learners work in groups in meaningful question and answer dialogues

Life skills: Effective communication as learners learn to ask and answer questions.

135

Link to other Learning Areas:

Learners engage in question and answer sessions using the Wh-words to their learning in Kiswahili and Kenyan Sign Language.
